channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over former CEO Jensen Huang's affair
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia on Thursday to investigate whether former CEO Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information. The probe also examines whether the company misled investors and the public regarding the risks. The investigation marks a significant legal escalation for Nvidia as state and federal regulators intensify scrutiny over the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's departure and export control compliance.

item.title: US Commerce Dept approved sales of over 879K AI chips to Chinese companies
item.description: The US Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies as of May 2026, according to disclosures released by House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast. The approvals included entities on the Department of Defense's Chinese military-linked list. This disclosure highlights the scale of US-approved AI chip sales to Chinese entities, including those linked to the military, amid scrutiny over export controls.

item.title: Google DeepMind institute outlines four pathways from AGI to ASI
item.description: Google DeepMind researchers published an essay outlining four pathways for AI development to move from human-level AGI to artificial general superintelligence (ASI). The essay notes that global effective compute has grown at least tenfold per year. For people following AI research, this framework maps out theoretical and technical pathways beyond human-level AGI toward superintelligence, alongside constraints and compute growth trends.

item.title: Anthropic raises $81.3B in record-breaking IPO as founders cash out $2B
item.description: Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising $81.3 billion in an initial public offering that included $1.95 billion for its seven founders. The stock closed at $97.17 per share, giving the company a valuation of roughly $1.7 trillion. The offering marks one of the largest public debuts in history, significantly expanding the capital and corporate backing available to a major AI lab while creating thousands of millionaire employees.

item.title: Nvidia in talks to acquire diffusion LLM startup Inception for $500M+
item.description: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for over $500 million plus earnouts. The discussions began prior to Jensen Huang's resignation. This move indicates Nvidia's ongoing acquisition activity and expansion into AI model development following leadership changes.

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
item.description: Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent designed to browse the web, work across apps, write code, and call services, according to a job listing. The project would put Apple in competition with similar AI assistants from Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. This move signals Apple's push into autonomous agentic AI assistants, aligning Siri and foundation model teams to compete with established rivals in device-control and cross-app automation.

item.title: Students sue school and police after chip bag triggers AI gun alert
item.description: Four high school students sued Baltimore County Public Schools, the police department, and Omnilert after an AI gun-detection system mistook a bag of chips for a firearm in October 2025. Despite school officials canceling the alert within two minutes, armed police were dispatched, resulting in the students being handcuffed and searched on campus. The case highlights the risks and real-world consequences when schools rely on automated surveillance technology that generates false alerts.

item.title: Bipartisan House lawmakers form AI Safety and Innovation Caucus
item.description: A bipartisan group of over two dozen House lawmakers formed the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus to balance mitigating AI risks with maintaining U.S. leadership in AI. The 26-member caucus includes seven Republicans and is co-chaired by Representatives George Whitesides, Nathaniel Moran, and Don Beyer. The formation of this bipartisan caucus signals that a growing faction in Congress intends to push for legislative guardrails on artificial intelligence despite the White House's opposition to heavy-handed regulation.

item.title: Google adds computer use to Gemini for macOS
item.description: Google added a computer use feature to the Gemini desktop app on macOS, enabling the AI to complete tasks across apps, files, and the web in the background. The feature is available in English to U.S. AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers. Google is bringing agentic desktop capabilities to its macOS application, matching similar offerings from competitors like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta.

item.title: Google introduces Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
item.description: Google released a Tool Retrieval feature in preview for the Gemini Interactions API to help agents manage large tool libraries. The feature loads tool parameter schemas on demand to reduce input token counts and latency. Tool Retrieval helps developers scale AI agents that rely on large libraries of software tools without inflating input token costs.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude model solves two open problems in black hole physics
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in black hole physics, including a calculation left unresolved for over 20 years. The model showed that black hole formation in very small universes happens through a sudden first-order phase transition. This demonstrates an AI model autonomously tackling and solving long-standing open problems in theoretical physics and quantum gravity.

item.title: Disseqt AI raises $8 million to expand enterprise AI governance platform
item.description: Disseqt AI, an Irish‑headquartered startup that provides testing and compliance tools for AI agents, secured $8 million in a funding round led by Gresham House Ventures. The capital will be used to grow its global enterprise customer base, open operations in London, and increase hiring in India. As more companies deploy AI agents that act on internal data, tools that verify safety, fairness and policy compliance become essential.

item.title: Anthropic’s $81.3 billion IPO tests AI’s circular financing model
item.description: Anthropic priced its shares at $83, raising $81.3 billion in the largest U.S. IPO to date and valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion. Supplier‑investors such as Amazon and Google hold stakes worth over $150 billion, highlighting the circular financing where the same firms fund and buy AI services. The deal shows how AI startups can rely on a loop of supplier‑investments rather than independent capital, reshaping financing and potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Sarvam AI’s Token Factory hosts mostly Chinese models on Indian GPUs, sparking sovereign AI debate
item.description: Sarvam AI launched its Token Factory inference platform on November 16, offering eight open-weight models via an OpenAI‑compatible API on GPU clusters in India, six of which are from Chinese firms. The company received a ₹98.68 crore government GPU subsidy for building indigenous models. It shows how government‑backed AI infrastructure can be used to run foreign models, raising questions about India’s goal of sovereign AI.

item.title: Study examines EU AI Act references on Hugging Face repository cards and discussions
item.description: Researchers conducted an empirical study of explicit references to the European Union's AI Act on Hugging Face using over five million records. They found that explicit references remain rare across all repository types. It provides empirical data on how practitioners are responding in practice to the EU AI Act on public AI sharing platforms.

item.title: Canva adds toggle to disable generative AI features for all users
item.description: Canva introduced a setting that lets free and paid users turn off most of its generative AI tools, including Magic Expand and AI image generation, while keeping non‑generative tools like background remover on. It gives designers control over AI assistance, addressing concerns about over‑automation and content provenance.

item.title: Karnataka hosts 1,088 GCCs and 111,000 AI/ML professionals, new report finds
item.description: A Zinnov-KDEM report released at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 found Karnataka hosts 1,088 global capability centres (51% of India's total) and 111,000 AI/ML professionals, with over 120 dedicated AI/ML Centres of Excellence. The report shows India's AI build-out is concentrating in one state, with Karnataka's GCCs moving from support roles to owning AI development for global enterprises.

item.title: IEA projects global data center investment to reach $4T by 2030
item.description: The International Energy Agency reported that global data center investments are expected to reach $4 trillion by 2030. The report also noted that fewer than 100 major AI projects would require a combined 50 gigawatts of power. The findings highlight how electricity generation, grid capacity, and equipment supply chains are becoming major bottlenecks for the expansion of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Early Anthropic investor Dustin Moskovitz says labs should slow down
item.description: Anthropic's early investor Dustin Moskovitz stated that he invested to promote safety rather than racing and that frontier AI labs should slow down. His stake from a 2021 investment is expected to be worth billions as Anthropic completes its public debut. The remarks highlight internal tensions among early backers regarding commercialization and safety as leading AI labs transition into publicly traded market giants.

item.title: AI agents redesign engineering parts with CAD parameters and simulations
item.description: Researchers showed that GPT-6 Astra can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations. Using a budget of 15 simulations, the AI lowered the strain in a magnesium stent's bends by 32%. This research demonstrates that large language models can coordinate changes across thousands of CAD parameters using simulation feedback, overcoming limitations of classical and industrial optimisers.

item.title: Instagram adds copyright detection tool for AI‑generated video copies
item.description: Meta announced that Instagram’s new Content Protection feature will scan Instagram and Facebook for visual matches and for videos that reuse a creator’s spoken words even when AI changes the visuals. The tool will be tested with a small group of creators in the coming weeks. It gives creators a way to curb AI‑generated deepfakes and reposts that steal their work and inflate engagement metrics.

item.title: Anthropic IPO retail investor allocation expected to fall below 20%
item.description: Sources expect Anthropic's IPO allocation for retail investors to fall below 20%. Retail buyers have historically received 5% to 10% of shares in large initial public offerings. It shows how intense demand for AI stocks is testing traditional Wall Street share allocation limits for individual investors.

item.title: Deutsche Telekom invests €100 million in French AI start-up Mistral
item.description: Deutsche Telekom's T.Capital Tech Fund invested €100 million in French artificial intelligence company Mistral. The investment marks a first step toward a strategic partnership to support companies and the public sector in Germany. The deal connects a major European telecommunications provider with one of Europe's leading artificial intelligence start-ups to expand regional enterprise AI adoption.

item.title: China's military seeks Nvidia chips for AI weapons, report says
item.description: A US congressional commission report states that China's People's Liberation Army is actively soliciting advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled weapons. The report highlights that Chinese-made processors continue to lag behind US rivals despite export controls. The findings underscore ongoing concerns about enforcement gaps in US semiconductor export controls as foreign military buyers attempt to acquire advanced American AI processors.

item.title: OpenAI and AMD cut chip design process to under five months using AI
item.description: OpenAI and AMD used AI models to optimize AMD's GPU architecture, reducing the chip design process from a year to under five months. The collaboration achieved up to 14% improvements in power, performance, and area. The collaboration demonstrates that AI models can successfully assist in complex hardware engineering tasks like rewriting register transfer level code to accelerate semiconductor development.

item.title: MegaRobo raises nearly $200 million for AI-driven lab automation
item.description: Beijing-based MegaRobo Technologies raised nearly $200 million in a financing round joined by the Oman Investment Authority. The capital will support core technology development, global expansion of its AI for Science business, and physical infrastructure. The funding highlights growing investment in physical AI infrastructure and automated laboratory systems for scientific research and drug discovery.

item.title: US lawmakers seek Microsoft briefing on reported ByteDance AI deal
item.description: A US House panel asked Microsoft to brief lawmakers on a reported $500 million deal allowing ByteDance to access OpenAI models via Azure. Lawmakers cited concerns over American companies helping China in the AI race. This development highlights growing congressional scrutiny over US technology business ties with Chinese firms and the distribution of advanced AI models.

item.title: Intel signs first outside customer for 18A chips
item.description: Intel signed its first outside customer for its 18A chips in a milestone for its foundry business. The external customer committed to Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node. This agreement marks a step in Intel's five-year effort to establish itself as a competitive chip manufacturer for external products.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon model for complex workflows
item.description: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Neon, a midtier model designed for software engineering, science, and knowledge work. Independent evaluations rank the model third overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 61. For AI observers, Neon's performance metrics demonstrate how midtier models are achieving results comparable to larger frontier systems while maintaining lower task costs.

item.title: Alibaba used regional companies to access Nvidia chips and aid military-linked lab
item.description: Alibaba used its AI computing technology to aid a lab linked to China's military by accessing Nvidia chips via regional companies like Megaspeed. Indonesian police raided Megaspeed's local unit in early 2026 at the request of U.S. authorities over suspicions of helping Chinese entities obtain restricted hardware. The revelations connect major technology firms and offshore data center operations directly to ongoing enforcement actions regarding U.S. chip export curbs to China.
